set.body:
Raised by independent review of the in-progress Epic 1 index. Measured on the working tree.

Verified good first

- .volume_ball_membership supports are EXACT vs brute force on six topologies their tests do not cover: full isotropic, anisotropic 1x1.5x2.5 spacing, random 35%-occupancy mask, two disconnected blocks, a single axial slab, and radius < spacing (self-only).
- The union co-occurrence pair pattern is EXACT vs brute force on full, sparse and slab masks (nnz 33935/12059/8844, all matching).
- Union degree is correctly reported as much larger than support size, which is what Epic 1 asked for: at r=6mm/p=50k, mean support 31.2 vs mean union degree 164.5 (5.3x).

The gap

.support_index_cost() and .support_index_preflight() have NO fold or evaluation-edge dimension - confirmed, no edges/folds/partition parameter anywhere in R/support-index.R. But the preflight emits a lowering DECISION:

  dense_metric_lowering = if (materialized_dense_metric_bytes <= workspace_bytes)
                            "materializable" else "support_streamed_only"

and materialized_dense_metric_bytes = 8 * sum(k_x^2) counts ONE metric per node.

Epic 5 and Epic 7 need K indexed by (support x evaluation edge). With leave-one-run-out over 8 runs that is ~8 training scopes, so the real requirement is ~8x what the preflight scores. Measured at p=50000, 3mm spacing, 4 GiB budget:

  r=4mm  mean|supp|=  6.8  union_deg= 22.8  dense_metric=0.05 GB  sum k^3=1.61e07  -> "materializable"
  r=6mm  mean|supp|= 31.2  union_deg=164.5  dense_metric=0.40 GB  sum k^3=1.58e09  -> "materializable"
  r=8mm  mean|supp|= 74.5  union_deg=412.2  dense_metric=2.10 GB  sum k^3=2.21e10  -> "materializable"

The r=8mm row is the problem. 2.10 GB fits 4 GiB and is reported materializable; at 8 folds the same configuration needs ~16.8 GB and does not. sum k^3 is likewise per-fold: 2.21e10 becomes 1.8e11 factorization units.

Why this matters beyond a wrong number

- Epic 8 acceptance says "No allocation scales as ... m times folds times k squared", but the only cost machinery in the codebase has no folds term, so nothing can check that criterion.
- Epic 8 sets a 4 GiB / 30 min go/no-go gate. If the gate is computed from this preflight it will pass configurations that cannot run.
- The decision is already consumed: benchmarks/run-support-index-benchmark.R:16,34 and tests/testthat/test-support-index.R:118,122.
- It interacts with bd-01KZXBDP92BNX44VWW08M35VQZ: if the metric handle only exposes apply_K, the coherent normalizer adds another sum k^3 per support PER EDGE, again unscored.

Suggested fix

Give .support_index_cost/.support_index_preflight an explicit evaluation-edge or training-scope multiplicity (default 1, and require callers in Epic 5/7 to pass the real value), report per-fold and total separately, and keep the lowering decision on the total. The index itself can stay fold-agnostic; the lowering decision cannot.
set.title: Support preflight emits a dense/streamed lowering decision that ignores the fold-edge dimension
